newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh faces severe power crisis.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh faces severe power crisis.

text.p: Bangladesh, now facing its worst power crisis, said on Saturday people might have to live in partial darkness until it built new power stations or revived old ones.
"We must stop wastage and economise on the use of available power to keep the wheels of the economy running," Energy Minister Nooruddin Khan said.
The government has already banned illumination for private ceremonies and weddings, and asked shops to close by 7.0 p.m. (1300 GMT), he told a news conference.
These moves followed the shutdown of several power stations due to shortages of natural gas, he said.
The government is under growing pressure from the opposition over persistent industrial and domestic power failures. Dhaka residents have staged street protests over the power cuts.
"The main reason for the shortfall in the gas supply is the closure of a large gas field due to years of excessive extractions," he said.
A 58-kilometre (40 mile) pipeline under a proposed national gas grid would infuse new life into the troubled power sector. "This will revive the closed power stations by April 30," Khan said.
"We have now opened up the energy sector for private investment," he said.
Government officials said eight foreign companies participated in the bidding for three barge-mounted power plants.
"The government may buy at $0.04 per unit of electricity from private companies," said one official.
Energy Secretary Tawfiq-e-Elahi Chowdury said there had been "tremendous response" from foreign firms for investment after the government prepared a private power policy.
"We are poor and we must attract foreign investment. We need money and time for implementaion of the projects in power sector," he said.
Khan said the Asian Development Bank committed $134 million and World Bank $50 million for refitting old power plants and setting up of new ones.
Germany has also offered $32 million for power transmission line beween Dhaka and southeastern Chittagong, he said.
Khan said: "We must develop more gas fields for generation of more electricity."
He said some 84 companies would make bids in London on March 24 and Houston, Texas, on March 31 for 15 gas exploration blocks in Bangladesh.
Khan said foreign investors were investing $550 million in eight such blocks by December this year.
